papers.title: OmniAssistBench: Assistant-style Interaction Benchmark for Omni-LLMs

summary.tldr: OmniAssistBench is a new benchmark for evaluating omni-modal LLMs as real-time video assistants using multi-turn video clips reverse-engineered from Internet videos.
key_points: Addresses non-deterministic interaction paths by feeding models predefined priors from source videos to constrain evaluation along specific routes.
Constructed via a multi-step pipeline requiring over 1,000 expert person-hours to deduce user goals and segment videos into multi-turn interaction clips.
Evaluated proprietary Gemini-3-Pro (scoring 66.4/100) against open-source Qwen3-Omni-Instruct (scoring 51.2/100).
Reveals key model failure modes: misinterpreting visual prompts like hand gestures, losing historical context over multiple turns, and failing to correctly time responses relative to target events.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a standardized methodology to evaluate real-time, interactive omni-modal models on active dynamic guidance tasks rather than passive video understanding.

papers.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts

summary.tldr: A two-step framework transfers optimal learning rates across model widths and extrapolates them to trillion-token training horizons using proxy models.
key_points: Formulates a Maximal Update Parameterization (̦P) adaptation specifically tailored for MoE architectures using Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and the Muon optimizer.
Establishes width-based learning rate transfer consistency alongside a predictive token-dimension scaling law.
Extrapolates optimal learning rates to massive training horizons up to 10 trillion tokens via linear regression on small proxy models with high fidelity (R^2 = 0.95).
Validated by pretraining a 155B total (17B active) parameter foundation model from scratch with stable training and low ablation costs.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need for expensive hyperparameter sweeps when training large-scale MoE models over massive token budgets.

papers.title: Graph Engineering in the Era of LLM Agents: From Individual Intelligence to System Intelligence

summary.tldr: Graph Engineering introduces explicit, dynamic graph structures representing tasks, agents, and system states to advance multi-agent LLM systems from individual to system intelligence.
key_points: Identifies limits in individual agent paradigms (Prompt, Context, Harness, and Loop Engineering) when managing complex, long-horizon tasks requiring heterogeneous expertise and persistent state.
Defines System Intelligence as the capability to organize, coordinate, and maintain execution states across multiple specialized agents toward a shared goal.
Establishes Graph Engineering to construct evolving graph abstractions for task decomposition, multi-agent orchestration, system dynamics modeling, and scalable agent evolution.
Curates open-source projects, datasets, and literature in a dedicated repository for research in graph-based agent systems.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides an architectural framework to scale AI systems beyond single-agent limits by using dynamic graphs to orchestrate specialized, interdependent agents.

papers.title: EviRank: Structured Relevance Evidence for Multimodal Image Re-ranking

summary.tldr: EviRank introduces a training-free framework that parses multimodal search queries into structured, six-slot evidence packages for transparent, constraint-based image re-ranking.
key_points: Parses text-only, image-only, or composed queries into typed criteria across six semantic slots (entities, attributes, relations) labeled as required, forbidden, or ignorable.
Re-ranks candidates via a training-free procedure combining deterministic rubric scoring with evidence-grounded listwise comparison.
Serves as structured supervision to distill a lightweight student model that retains over 90% of the teacher model's capability at lower computational cost.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance across five benchmarks for text-to-image, image-to-image, and composed image retrieval.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates opaque embeddings and hallucinatory chain-of-thought outputs by recasting multimodal image re-ranking as verifiable, fine-grained semantic constraint satisfaction.

papers.title: InfinityEdit: Infinite Video Editing with a Lightweight Edit-Ignition Adapter

summary.tldr: InfinityEdit introduces a lightweight edit-ignition adapter that enables streaming video generators to process unbounded, sequential edit instructions on open-ended video streams without relying on fixed-length, frame-by-frame static inputs.
key_points: Addresses infinite video editing where models must generate future segments that continue an open-ended stream while applying incoming edit requests.
Uses a lightweight adapter with history cross-attention for frame guidance, temporal causal self-attention for unidirectional temporal flow, and edit cross-attention to inject instructions.
Activates the adapter exclusively during the chunk where an edit instruction arrives, returning subsequent chunks to the base model with a reset anchor frame.
Includes a specialized data-collection pipeline designed specifically for infinite video editing tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows real-time, continuous video editing for open-ended streams—such as live game restyling—without quality degradation as edits accumulate over time.

papers.title: AgentMercury: Your Agent Can Synthesize Verifiable Environments for Business Scenarios at scale

summary.tldr: AgentMercury synthesizes verifiable, executable business environments at scale to train AI agents via reinforcement learning using scenario-grounded world models instead of predefined task benchmarks.
key_points: Generates executable environments featuring persistent entities, services, tools, states, and cross-service invariants across 14 industries and 50 countries.
Used to construct 4,783 executable environments that serve as reinforcement learning training substrates for policy models.
Post-training, Qwen3.5-4B improved performance from 12.3 to 15.7 on EnterpriseOps-GYM and from 45.9 to 56.0 on AIME26.
Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on construction traces increased executable-world authoring success on held-out scenarios from 3.3% to 83.3%.
summary.why_it_matters: Training agents on auto-generated business environments improves generalizability across enterprise workflows, reasoning, coding, and tool-use tasks without relying on target-specific benchmarks.

papers.title: Towards Faithful Simulation of Human Shopping Behavior

summary.tldr: RecVerse is a GUI-grounded user simulation agent that uses a cognitive hierarchical memory and a trajectory-level RL objective to produce realistic multi-turn e-commerce shopping sessions.
key_points: Addresses the Memory Challenge using a hierarchical structure comprising Working Memory, Episodic Memory, and Preference Memory, where memory updates are learned as actions.
Addresses the Optimization Challenge via trajectory-level reinforcement learning that scores full sessions to align macro action-type distributions and micro intent with real users.
Operates as a visual agent perceiving e-commerce web pages directly through screenshots.
Introduces USB (User Simulation Benchmark), an interactive e-commerce GUI trajectory dataset designed for multi-turn user simulation evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: It improves the fidelity of offline evaluation and reinforcement learning environments for e-commerce recommendation systems by mitigating common simulation errors like over-exploration and passivity.

papers.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment

summary.tldr: CLEAR uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to continuously scale a safety LoRA adapter's activation, preserving base LLM utility while reducing harmful responses.
key_points: Uses a lightweight hidden-state gating mechanism to continuously control safety adapter activation strength.
Keeps the underlying LLM backbone frozen to prevent utility degradation on benign prompts.
Reduces Llama-3-8B-Instruct HarmBench Attack Success Rate (ASR) from 32.3% to 0.5%.
Outperforms global SFT and standard LoRA on GSM8K accuracy by up to 7.1 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: It offers a conditional routing approach to safety alignment that maintains model robustness against harmful prompts without compromising performance on general reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Llama-Mobile: Efficient 2.7-Bit Quantization of VLMs

summary.tldr: Llama-Mobile introduces a quantization framework that uses self-generated training data to compress Vision-Language Models into a novel 2.7-bit-per-parameter format optimized for Arm CPUs.
key_points: Uses the VLM itself to generate training data for the quantization pipeline, eliminating the need for the original training setup.
Introduces a 2.7-bit-per-parameter weight format designed for efficient execution on Arm CPUs.
Compresses the Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct model to 3.7 GB using 8-bit activations while preserving performance on visual question answering benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the deployment of large 11B parameter Vision-Language Models directly on resource-constrained mobile hardware with Arm CPUs.

papers.title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference

summary.tldr: Daedalus-150M is a 150M-parameter convolution-attention hybrid LLM designed specifically for CPU inference that outperforms larger baseline models while decoding up to 2.08x faster at a 2048-token context length.
key_points: Uses full attention in only 6 of 18 blocks, relying on short convolutions with a 2-timestep memory state for the remaining 12 blocks to eliminate KV-cache re-reading.
Trained from scratch on 59.9B tokens, achieving a 47.31 score on a five-task benchmark and a 0.8685 validation bits-per-byte.
Outperforms GPT-2 124M, Pythia-160M, OPT-125M, GPT-neo-125M, and MobileLLM-125M despite using significantly less training data.
Compared to an identical-size all-attention model, the hybrid yielded a 0.81% higher quality metric, a 6.3% smaller 4-bit file, and 1.76x faster decoding at 2048 tokens.
Identified failure modes including unmitigated 4-bit quantization quality loss, ~50% inert convolution channels, and an oversized vocabulary.
summary.why_it_matters: By restricting attention to a fraction of layers, hybrid architectures can drastically reduce the memory and compute overhead of long context lengths on standard CPUs.

papers.title: From Attention Masks to Inert Zero-Vector Tokens: OAttention and O-Closure for Token Dynamics

summary.tldr: OAttention introduces an active-presence coefficient based on hidden-carrier norm that turns zero-vector tokens into non-participating inert elements while establishing compositional O-Closure across transformer blocks.
key_points: Assigns an active-presence coefficient p_i = ||h_i||^2 / (tau + ||h_i||^2) to token carriers, gating emitted information and weighting shared computations.
OAttention applies p_i to gate receiver outputs and weights source tokens by p_j in both the attention numerator and partition function.
Defines local O-components (OFFN, ONorm, OInject, OStandardize) that satisfy the O-Closure law M(H + 0) = M(H) + 0, enabling full OTransformer composition.
Zero-fine-tuning retrofits of TabPFN v3 regressor yielded mean RMSE changes of +0.088% (OAttention) and +0.177% (Full-O) across 18 evaluation cases.
A two-block ablation confirmed that OAttention requires the full OTransformer path to preserve NULL states through host model components.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables mathematically exact null-token dynamics and inert zero-vector insertions without altering standard attention scoring or requiring retraining from scratch.

papers.title: Don't Solve, Just Compare: Tiny Advisors for Runtime Intervention in LLM Agents

summary.tldr: Comparison-Only Tiny Advisor (COTA) improves LLM agent reliability by using a small model to compare candidate continuations and supply non-binding advice without needing full task-solving capabilities.
key_points: COTA replaces expert solvers and heavy task-capable critics with a small comparator that evaluates whether sampled alternative steps outperform the actor's initial proposal.
The comparator is trained via pairwise supervision derived from same-prefix counterfactual execution branches.
When intervention is triggered through repeated comparisons, preferred alternatives are provided as non-binding advice to let the original actor replan.
Evaluated across WebShop, ALFWorld, and tau^3-Retail using three different base actors, COTA improved performance across all nine test configurations compared to baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that runtime intervention can enhance LLM agent performance using lightweight auxiliary models that possess significantly less task-solving capacity than the primary actor.

papers.title: Jacobian-guided Noise Injection for Quantization Robustness in Large Language Models

summary.tldr: A training strategy injects zero-mean Gaussian noise into pre-attention logits using variance derived from the softmax Jacobian Frobenius norm to improve LLM post-training quantization robustness.
key_points: Identifies the softmax operator as the primary bottleneck for quantization stability due to outlier sensitivity and a state-dependent Jacobian.
Theoretically proves that suppressing the softmax Jacobian norm bounds performance degradation caused by discretization errors.
Injects Gaussian noise into pre-attention logits scaled directly by local attention sensitivity rather than relying on heuristics or direct Jacobian penalties.
Achieves up to a 37% relative gain in Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K for SigLIP and up to a 40% relative perplexity improvement on WikiText in low-bit quantization regimes.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables lower-bit quantization of vision and language transformers with significantly less performance degradation by stabilizing the self-attention mechanism during training.

papers.title: Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training

summary.tldr: E$^2$-TTT uses a derived closed-form state transition to achieve parallelized chunk-wise training that exactly matches the per-token fast-weight and momentum updates of Test-Time Training.
key_points: Derives a closed-form state transition under the chunk-start weight gradient approximation to match end-of-chunk per-token recurrence states.
Preserves temporal update structures discarded by prior chunk-wise TTT methods while maintaining high training throughput.
Validated on models up to 1.3B parameters trained from scratch, matching baselines in language modeling and improving in-context retrieval.
Demonstrates length extrapolation on the Needle in a Haystack passkey test, maintaining over 90% accuracy at 8x the training context length.
summary.why_it_matters: It eliminates the tradeoff between per-token expressivity and chunk-wise hardware efficiency in Test-Time Training architectures.

papers.title: Nothing Changed but the Model: CellFill -- Bounded In-Cell Learning for Bit-Identical, Revocable Updates to Quantized LLMs

summary.tldr: CellFill achieves bit-identical, revocable LLM updates by training bounded per-weight residuals strictly within the dequantization gap of frozen 4-bit quantization cells.
key_points: Modifications are written strictly to per-weight residuals within quantization decision cells, guaranteeing bit-for-bit equivalence to the original release artifact upon re-quantization.
Across paired seeds, the constrained dense path matches unconstrained reference performance on fact recall (58.9% vs 59.3%) while delivering superior held-out cross-domain perplexity.
CellFill acts as a structural trust region that mitigates cross-domain forgetting compared to unmerged adapters, though it cannot repair diverged training runs.
Successfully validated on a 27B parameter hybrid linear-attention model across 2.4e10 constrained weights, requiring half the cross-domain perplexity cost for matched recall compared to a 1.7B model.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows deployed quantized models to incorporate new knowledge without invalidating prior evaluations, breaking KV caches, or altering base model checkpoints.

papers.title: SAC-Copula: Quality-Preserving Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models via Smooth Correlated Gumbel Fields

summary.tldr: SAC-Copula introduces smooth, locally correlated Gumbel perturbation fields via a Gaussian copula to watermark diffusion language models without degrading generation quality.
key_points: Replaces position-wise i.i.d. perturbations with smooth, locally correlated Gumbel fields constructed via a Gaussian copula to align with iterative parallel unmasking.
Includes a SAC-aware detector featuring covariance-aware filtering and native-sample calibration.
Reduces latent perturbation roughness to match iterative refinement dynamics, improving perplexity (PPL) tail stability on Dream-7B over i.i.d. baselines.
Demonstrates improved quality-detectability trade-offs on LLaDA and robust low-FPR detection under token-edit stress tests.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables reliable detection of text generated by diffusion language models while preserving generation quality and stability during iterative refinement.

papers.title: Memory Augmentation Unlocks Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

summary.tldr: A training-free framework called Memory-Augmented Compression retrieves historical reasoning patterns to prefill context, enabling compressed Chain-of-Thought reasoning without sacrificing accuracy.
key_points: Formalizes the Context-Generation Substitution Law, which states that prefill-side explicit reasoning context can substitute for decode-time generation length.
Constructs reusable reasoning memories summarizing patterns, constraints, and critical operations from past traces rather than using raw demonstrations.
Outperforms standard Chain-of-Draft (CoD) by 21.4, 28.0, 29.5, and 6.61 accuracy points on GSM8K, MATH, BBH, and MMLU-Sci respectively.
Achieves a 1.14x to 1.49x latency speedup over standard Chain-of-Thought (CoT) while remaining compatible with token-level, trace-level, and inference-state compression mechanisms.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large language models to perform complex reasoning tasks significantly faster and with lower decode-time overhead while improving accuracy over existing compression methods.

papers.title: RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

summary.tldr: RARE enables effective representation steering in MoE language models by projecting behavioral perturbations onto the router matrix's null space to maintain expert routing consistency.
key_points: Identifies that direct representation engineering fails in MoEs due to routing drift caused by hidden state perturbations.
Projects behavioral perturbations onto the null space of the router matrix to remove router-visible components and corrects downstream layer routing drift.
Evaluated five perturbation estimators across six open-weight MoE models on harmfulness, truthfulness, and factual editing tasks.
Achieved 53.3% attack success rate on harmfulness while retaining 67.8% MMLU accuracy, improved TruthfulQA MC1 accuracy from 41.0% to 58.6%, and increased CounterFact efficacy from 16.8% to 96.3%.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows lightweight inference-time control of MoE models without causing performance degradation from broken expert routing.

papers.title: Sparse Token Routing in Efficient Transformers

summary.tldr: Evaluating the SEWN two-stream Transformer shows that learned sparse token routing yields negligible accuracy gains over parameter-matched baselines, though contextual gates produce robust token-importance signals.
key_points: SEWN uses a learned gate to route tokens to either a lightweight stream or a full-capacity stream.
End-to-end experiments demonstrate negligible accuracy changes when using routing compared to parameter-matched baselines.
A static lexicon-seeded prior fails counterfactual faithfulness testing on BoolQ.
A fully contextual gate yields statistically significant token-importance separation (p < 10^-10) on evaluated tasks without impacting overall accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings challenge the assumption that dynamic token routing improves Transformer performance efficiency over simpler parameter-matched baselines.

papers.title: Open-Weight Masked Introspection: Measuring What Language Models Can Report About Their Own Computation

summary.tldr: Researchers developed the Open-Weight Masked Introspection framework to test model self-auditing across eight open-weight models, finding zero intrinsic ability to verbally report internal computational interventions.
key_points: Evaluated 8 open-weight models across 78,000 measurements by intervening on residual streams, attention heads, and sparse-autoencoder features against sham and impact-matched controls.

Unfine-tuned models failed to discriminate real interventions from sham runs in their verbal reports, yielding an AUROC of ~0.5007 with an equivalence test bounding the effect below 0.15 percentage points.

Internal activations contained the requisite information: linear probes achieved 75% to 95.8% accuracy (improving to 0% held-out error at the final layer), and fine-tuning enabled near-perfect intervention reporting.
One model implicitly encoded the intervention signal in its output confidence scores (AUROC 0.647) despite invariant yes/no verbal output text.
summary.why_it_matters: Safety oversight mechanisms cannot rely on a model's untuned verbal self-reports to detect internal state changes or tampering, requiring internal probing or explicit calibration instead.

papers.title: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding

summary.tldr: LiLiCorr improves speculative decoding draft coherence by using lightweight in/out vector cosine similarity across top-k candidates to select jointly coherent token blocks.
key_points: Addresses joint incoherence in diffusion-style block drafters (e.g., DFlash) trained on per-position marginals by scoring adjacent top-k token candidates using cosine similarity of in/out vectors.
Computes candidate pairwise match scores in parallel via batched matrix operations in a single lightweight network pass, leaving only a low-cost sequential greedy walk.
Co-trains the drafter alongside LiLiCorr to encourage proposals that yield longer accepted sequence lengths.
Increases DFlash acceptance length by 9% to 19% across all benchmarks, with the scoring head adding approximately 2.8% to per-block latency.
Outperformed DFlash and two concurrent coherence methods in throughput across 70 of 72 evaluation settings, including long-context inputs an order of magnitude beyond its training length.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables significantly higher inference throughput for speculative decoding with diffusion-style drafters at a negligible latency cost of under 3%.

papers.title: Re$^3$Cap: Retrieval-Guided Refinement for Image Captioning Enhancement via Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Re3Cap introduces a retrieval-guided reasoning strategy that uses multi-modal retrieval to guide reinforcement learning for image captioning without additional annotations.
key_points: Uses a Caption Refinement Suggester (CRS) and Caption Quality Assessor (CQA) to detect and correct hallucinations and omissions in generated captions.
Leverages multi-modal retrieval as a reasoning signal to bridge the performance gap between reinforcement learning (RL) and Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT).
Outperforms GRPO with an average improvement of 8.64% in relation reasoning on the COCO-LN500 benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables Large Vision-Language Models to generate more detailed and accurate captions via reinforcement learning without relying on additional human annotations.

papers.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment

summary.tldr: CLEAR introduces a conditional safety adaptation framework that uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to continuously scale the activation strength of a safety LoRA adapter, optimizing the safety-utility trade-off.
key_points: Uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to dynamically route and control the activation strength of a safety low-rank adapter without modifying the frozen backbone.
Reduces HarmBench Attack Success Rate (ASR) on Llama-3-8B-Instruct from 32.3% down to 0.5%.
Outperforms globally applied SFT and standard LoRA on utility metrics, achieving up to 7.1 percentage points higher accuracy on GSM8K.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that dynamic, input-conditional adapter routing can preserve model performance on benign tasks while effectively mitigating harmful completions.

papers.title: Utility Under Attack: Agent Memory Poisoning and the Limits of Content Screening and Provenance Ranking

summary.tldr: A study demonstrates that unoptimized false assertions in 1.2% of a agent memory corpus reduce retrieval accuracy from 0.850 to 0.300, while bypassing content screening and breaking additive provenance ranking.
key_points: Poisoning 1.2% of a LongMemEval corpus with single-pass, unoptimized false assertions drops task accuracy from 0.850 to 0.300.
A four-stage write-time screening pipeline that achieved 0.832 recall on indirect prompt injection failed completely, rejecting 0 out of 360 poisoned memories.

Additive provenance weighting fails (p=0.80): weights strong enough to suppress query-shaped poison also suppress valid untrusted evidence, dropping accuracy to 0.0417 when answers rely on untrusted sources.
Authors advocate for bounded occupancy constraints during retrieval rather than content-only screening or additive provenance penalties.
summary.why_it_matters: Simple memory poisoning attacks easily bypass standard safety guardrails and reveal fundamental flaws in relying on additive provenance weights to secure persistent LLM memory.

papers.title: Personalized Privacy Control in LLMs via Attention Head Intervention

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce personalized privacy for LLMs, evaluate prompt failures via P3Bench, and propose REPAIR, an inference-time attention head intervention method to enforce user-specific disclosure preferences.
key_points: P3Bench extends contextual privacy policies by adding user-specific disclosure preferences to evaluate LLM privacy control.
Standard prompt-based policies fail to enforce personalized privacy, yielding policy ignorance ratios of 51.25% in Qwen2.5-7B and 74.28% in Gemma3-4B.
REPAIR applies robust inference-time interventions on attention heads to adjust model behavior toward policy-consistent outputs without retraining.
summary.why_it_matters: System prompts alone are insufficient to prevent LLM agents from leaking sensitive user data, making internal mechanistic interventions like REPAIR necessary for reliable privacy enforcement.

security.title: AID-Guard: Stateful Authorization for Delegated Agent Effects

summary.tldr: AID-Guard introduces a stateful authorization-to-effect closure protocol that prevents duplicate or unauthorized provider actions during agent retries, races, and crash recovery.
key_points: Revalidates approved requests and provider states at commit, maintaining a single reservation under ambiguity until a terminal result or certified no-effect delivery fence is achieved.
Blocked 44/44 attacks under complete proposer compromise and 20/20 post-admission lifecycle attacks in a composition study.
Completed 210 Stripe trials, 40 terminalize-successor schedules, 30 overlapping races, and 10 crash-recovery schedules across Stripe and Resend with zero duplicate effects.
Evaluated via a Python/SQLite prototype in a loopback Model Context Protocol (MCP) domain where 13 live mutations produced no unauthorized provider effects.
Replacing a strict exact-manifest profile (which reduced benign utility by 35.4–43.8 percentage points) with a typed frontier recovered 9–10 completions without introducing unsafe effects.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes the first evaluated agent-authorization protocol that ensures idempotency and authorization integrity across the complete lifecycle of delegated tool-using AI actions.

security.title: BackDFL: A Unified Benchmark For Backdoor Attacks and Defenses In Decentralized Federated Learning

summary.tldr: BackDFL is a unified benchmark designed to systematically evaluate Decentralized Federated Learning robustness under realistic and adaptive backdoor attacks.
key_points: Critiques existing DFL robustness studies for using simplified threat models, ad hoc configurations, and inconsistent topologies.
Reveals that Byzantine-robust DFL methods and adapted FL defenses fail with malicious participant rates as low as 15%.
Demonstrates that DFL defense robustness varies substantially across different communication graph topologies, particularly in heterogeneous settings.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that DFL security is overstated and provides a standardized framework to develop defenses against persistent backdoor attacks in serverless environments.

security.title: TraceGrant: A Contract-Governed Security Framework for the Task-Effect Lifecycle of Networked LLM Agents

summary.tldr: TraceGrant is a security framework that governs networked LLM agent workflows by establishing pre-execution task-effect boundaries via a Contract, constraining runtime tool authority, and verifying post-execution task completion.
key_points: Uses a Contract derived from trusted user requests to define the task-effect boundary before execution begins.
Restricts runtime evidence and tool calls to instantiating only the specific authority explicitly pre-established by the Contract.
Verifies final task completion against actual tool execution results to prevent redirected or altered persistent external effects.
Achieved zero successful attacks on 949 AgentDojo and 400 Agent Security Bench attack cases under fixed benchmark settings with attack rates of 77.32% and 83.00%.
summary.why_it_matters: It unifies trusted intent, runtime evidence, and tool execution into a single lifecycle framework to neutralize indirect prompt injections in networked LLM agents.

security.title: ClawSentry: A Progressive Multi-Tier Security Monitor for Safeguarding Autonomous LLM Agents

summary.tldr: ClawSentry is an open-source, framework-agnostic security gateway that uses a progressive multi-tier decision engine and session tracking to safeguard autonomous LLM agents across four control loop loci.
key_points: Defends four lifecycle loci: skill admission (FSPR), invocation-time intent (L1-L3 engine), execution-time effect (session anti-bypass), and post-action consequence.
Employs a three-tier runtime engine combining a deterministic L1 layer, a rule-anchored L2 semantic reviewer, and a read-only L3 evidence-seeking agent.
Uses an Agent Harness Protocol (AHP) abstraction to enforce uniform policies across Codex, Claude Code, Kimi CLI, and Gemini CLI without altering agent internals.
Reduces contextual Attack Success Rate (ASR) on SkillInject with Codex/GPT-5.4 from 39.55% to 2.61% with negligible impact on Task Success Rate (83.78% to 83.05%).
Confines ASR to 9.09-15.03% (down from 33.5-49.7%) across five Work Agents on the SkillsSafety benchmark while maintaining a 98.7% aggregate clean TSR.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a cross-framework mechanism to drastically reduce malicious prompt and skill injection attacks in autonomous agents without significantly decreasing task completion performance.

security.title: Trustworthy RAG: An Evaluation Agent for Detecting Misinformation and Knowledge Poisoning in Generative AI Systems

summary.tldr: An Evaluation Agent middleware mitigates RAG knowledge poisoning using NLI factual verification, five-signal poison detection, and a non-linearly dampened Trust Index to evaluate retrieved context prior to LLM generation.
key_points: Uses a composite Trust Index formula T = 0.4F + 0.35C + 0.25(1 - P) featuring a non-linear dampener designed for high-contamination contexts.
Achieved 91% accuracy, 100% precision, and 100% recall on instruction injection using Llama 3.3 70B on TruthfulQA, while subtle in-place edits like entity swaps proved harder to detect.
Demonstrated cross-model discrimination with ROC-AUC scores between 0.73 and 0.81 across three LLMs, indicating generation style impacts performance more than model size.
Secured an OWASP/CWE software-engineering coding assistant against instruction injection attacks containing unsafe advice with a 92% F1 score.
summary.why_it_matters: Filtering poisoned or contradictory contexts before LLM generation prevents RAG systems from inadvertently consuming and propagating malicious misinformation.

security.title: Structured but Fragile: On the Limits of LLMs in Cybersecurity Decision-Making

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated LLMs on budget-constrained defense selection over real-world attack graphs, finding that LLMs can approximate structured security reasoning under explicit representations but remain highly fragile to framing, complexity, and prompt variations.
key_points: Evaluated LLM defense selection strategies across diverse threat scenarios (ransomware, supply-chain, cloud, Kubernetes, POS malware, ICS/OT) against a game-theoretic optimization baseline.
Providing explicit attack-graph structures enables LLMs to produce strategies near the baseline, but performance degrades as graph complexity increases.

LLM evaluators exhibit non-monotonic risk judgment, fail to consistently rank near-optimal strategies highest, and are vulnerable to framing bias, such as rating a poor strategy dramatically higher when relabeled as 'optimal'.

When prompted to generate code solvers for the defense optimization problem, LLMs produce the correct high-level formulation but yield implementations with poor computational scaling relative to purpose-built solvers.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that relying on LLMs for autonomous security decision-making is risky because their apparent reasoning capabilities are fragile and easily disrupted by prompt framing and graph scale.

security.title: Vibe Coding and Web Application Security: A Twin-Prompt Study

summary.tldr: A study shows that appending explicit security requirements to LLM web application prompts reduced confirmed vulnerabilities from 51 to 24 across six applications generated by an agentic coding assistant.
key_points: Evaluated six web applications in two prompt variants (baseline vs. security-aware) generated in a single, non-iterative round by the same model and agentic assistant.
Combined static, dependency, dynamic, and manual security analysis to yield 75 confirmed findings out of 85 candidate issues.
The security-aware prompt variant contained zero Critical or High issues, with its most severe finding discovered only through manual testing.
summary.why_it_matters: Explicitly prompting LLMs with security requirements can substantially lower the severity and frequency of vulnerabilities in AI-generated web applications.

security.title: Uncovering and Understanding Hidden Dependencies in the LLM API Reseller Ecosystem via Prefix-Cache Side Channels

summary.tldr: Researchers developed CacheTracer, an API-only side-channel tool leveraging prefix-cache reuse to uncover hidden upstream dependencies and multi-level supply chains among LLM API resellers.
key_points: CacheTracer uses two primitives: 'Flood' to populate cache state through one endpoint, and 'Prove' to test if another endpoint reuses that state without triggering self-induced hits.
A study of 39 reseller endpoints and 636 pairs across 1.1 million requests revealed that 37.1% of measured pairs shared cache reach.
The recovered dependency graphs revealed containment hierarchies spanning up to seven layers, with a single cache reach contained within at least 31 other nodes.
Experiments showed that the recovered cache-reach structures are model-specific and highly reliable across real-world and controlled environments.
summary.why_it_matters: Opaque, deeply nested reseller supply chains create massive blast radiuses where a single compromised upstream provider can silently inspect or modify traffic across dozens of downstream services.

security.title: The Claws in Plain Sight: Unauthorized Context Disclosure through LLM Agent Tool Calls

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced 'Claw in Plain Sight,' an authority-pressure attack that tricks LLM agents into transmitting protected contextual data within legitimate tool-call arguments.
key_points: The attack uses task-adjacent content to frame protected user profile attributes as procedurally necessary for generated tool arguments.
A benchmark evaluation crossing six pressure levels and four privacy-policy levels across five DeepSeek and Claude configurations produced session-level disclosure rates between 20.8% and 75.0%.
Stronger prompt-level privacy instructions reduced aggregate disclosure but failed to eliminate it consistently, demonstrating that system prompts are not portable security boundaries.
Testing measured policy-violating generation at the local context-to-argument boundary using synthetic profiles, rather than live network exfiltration.
summary.why_it_matters: The findings highlight the necessity of implementing destination- and purpose-aware inspection of generated tool arguments before execution rather than relying solely on prompt-based privacy guardrails.

security.title: Beyond End-to-End Success: Diagnosing Failures in Long-Horizon Security LLM Agents

summary.tldr: A diagnostic methodology for long-horizon security LLM agents uses checkpoints and controlled interventions to isolate upstream bottleneck failures from capability failures before task completion.
key_points: Evaluates four long-horizon task families: delayed information reuse, observed state reuse, strategy recovery, and decision-making under uncertainty.
Checkpoint analysis reveals many Gemini 2.5 Flash failures happen before the model ever observes the state required for downstream reuse.
In a 92-seed study, protocol-disambiguation guidance increased Gemini 2.5 Flash state observation from 65.5% to 95.4%, but the same intervention yielded opposite results on Gemini 3.7 Flash.
Gemini 3.7 Flash demonstrated that state observation no longer reliably predicts final task completion, highlighting shifting failure modes across model generations.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying solely on end-to-end task success masks true model capabilities, making fine-grained failure diagnosis necessary to fix upstream bottlenecks in multi-step security workflows.

security.title: aiXamine: Unified Black-Box Evaluation of Cross-Dimensional Trade-offs in LLM Safety, Security, and Privacy

summary.tldr: aiXamine is a unified black-box platform that evaluates LLM safety, security, and privacy as interdependent properties, revealing critical cross-dimensional trade-offs across 120+ models.
key_points: Evaluates LLMs using an automated red-teaming pipeline with 46 tests across nine services, generating hierarchical risk profiles and cross-service trade-off analytics.
Demonstrates a safety tax where stronger alignment systematically increases over-refusal, such as scoring 99.3 in safety while rejecting one-third of benign queries.
Shows that privacy is near-orthogonal to safety and security, meaning standard alignment techniques fail to capture or guarantee privacy protections.

Formally characterizes distillation-induced robustness collapse, where off-policy distillation without on-policy correction dropped robustness from 56.9 to 2.6 on identical base architectures due to entropy collapse.
summary.why_it_matters: Single-axis LLM evaluation misses critical trade-offs, proving that optimizing models for safety or performance can actively undermine security, utility, and privacy.

security.title: AEGIS: Preventing Cross-Domain Resource Abuse in MCP

summary.tldr: AEGIS is a policy enforcement framework that uses LLMs to normalize heterogeneous Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool invocations, enabling fine-grained protection against cross-domain resource abuse.
key_points: Addresses resource abuse vectors (such as oversized search radii or long video requests) caused by multimodal MCP tools across text, image, video, and location modalities.
Uses LLM reasoning to analyze, categorize, and normalize diverse tool request schemas into a unified representation for policy evaluation.
Integrates with Open Policy Agent (OPA) and the ContextForge AI Gateway to enforce fine-grained security constraints without breaking agent flexibility.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents denial-of-service and backend resource exhaustion caused by malicious or unconstrained LLM agent tool calls across diverse schemas.

security.title: Masking Is Not Enough: Generative Restoration for Multimodal De-Identification in Medical AI

summary.tldr: ClinX introduces an end-to-end multimodal medical de-identification framework combining OCR-based masking, generative image restoration (ClinX-PRISM), and progressive text sanitization to protect PHI while maintaining MedVQA utility.
key_points: Image-side PHI sanitization uses OCR to detect visible identifiers, creates binary masks, and applies ClinX-PRISM, a no-skip generative restoration module with privacy-oriented post-processing.
Text-side PHI is mitigated via three progressive levels: regex masking, context-aware masking, and rewrite-based sanitization.
Evaluations in MedVQA show OCR-only masking is insufficient, whereas generative restoration better preserves visual context while sharply reducing recoverable PHI.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that simple redaction degrades downstream AI performance, offering a generative approach to safely share multimodal medical data without sacrificing task utility.

security.title: $Z^2$-ACT: End-to-End Verifiable Agentic Intent Control for Open 6G RAN

summary.tldr: Z²-ACT introduces an end-to-end architecture for Open 6G RAN that integrates agentic coordination, formal intent constraints, zero-trust prompt verification, and zero-knowledge proofs across non-RT and near-RT RICs.
key_points: Integrates four core primitives across non-real-time (non-RT) and near-real-time (near-RT) RICs: agentic coordination, formal intent constraints, zero-trust prompt verification, and cryptographic accountability.
Uses a live LLM in the non-RT path to translate operator goals into typed Intent Contracts, passing LLM inputs only after adversarial intent checking.
Releases skill sequences via a self-management gate and logs successful commits as binding commitments using zero-knowledge proofs.

Validated on public ColO-RAN measurements and KPM sequences, outperforming targeted ablations and conventional reinforcement learning baselines in attack resilience and actuation filtering within near-RT latency budgets.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables safe, verifiable, and cryptographically auditable multi-vendor AI control loops in open 6G architectures without compromising real-time performance constraints.

security.title: Chat First, Worry Later: Understanding Individuals' Privacy Perceptions Using ChatGPT in a Work Context

summary.tldr: A study of 224 workers reveals organizational policies boost privacy-related ChatGPT proficiency, while unguided privacy concerns significantly suppress the frequency and diversity of GenAI usage.
key_points: Survey evaluated N=224 participants across multiple employment sectors (education, healthcare, IT) using ChatGPT in their work routines.
Organizational policies for GenAI show a statistically significant positive association with users' privacy-related ChatGPT proficiency.
Overall user proficiency regarding ChatGPT privacy remains low across surveyed sectors.
High general privacy concerns decrease both usage frequency and task diversity, particularly in organizations lacking formal GenAI policies.
summary.why_it_matters: Organizations must establish formal GenAI usage policies to improve employee privacy proficiency and prevent unmanaged privacy fears from stifling productive tool adoption.

infra.title: VeRL-Omni v0.2.0: Faster Diffusion RL and Stable Omni Training

summary.tldr: VeRL-Omni v0.2.0 accelerates diffusion RL and stabilizes omni-modal training by introducing request-level batching in vLLM-Omni and a V1 trainer architecture.
key_points: Replaced serial B≈1 DiT rollout forwards with request-level batching, packing multiple complete requests into single transformer forwards.
Integrated a V1 trainer path for diffusion RL, laying the foundation for decoupled rollout and training execution.
Increased GPU utilization from ~80% to ~100% on the Qwen-Image FlowGRPO LoRA recipe, reducing isolated generation time from 226s to 108s (a 52% reduction).
Resolved correctness issues involving request-batched diffusion log-probs, async rollout semantics, rank-local LoRA weight updates, and rollout-correction hooks.
summary.why_it_matters: The performance and architectural upgrades significantly reduce rollout latency and compute costs for high-dimensional diffusion post-training and RLHF workloads.

vendors.title: Anthropic’s best AI model struggles to attract users as cheaper tools thrive

summary.tldr: Anthropic's July 2026 annualized revenue reached $65bn, but enterprise spending data reveals high costs are hindering adoption of its flagship Fable 5 model relative to older variants like Opus 4.8.
key_points: Anthropic reported $65bn in annualized revenue for July 2026, up from $47bn in May, with 6,000 enterprise customers spending at least $100,000 annually.
OpenAI's annualized revenue rose 35% in the quarter to cross $40bn, driven by the July release of GPT 5.6.
Ramp AI index billing data shows Opus 4.8 dominated Anthropic model spend in July at 28.0%, while Fable 5 captured only 8.0% due to cost constraints.
Newer models Opus 5 (released July 24th) and Sonnet 5 accounted for 3.5% and 3.6% of spending, respectively.
summary.why_it_matters: Enterprise LLM spending is heavily cost-sensitive, driving higher utilization of previous-generation or cheaper models over newly released flagship offerings.
